core_obligations: Reduce the triviality of the divisor to a claim (proof lines 1269-1281): given an invertible module whose associated divisor class is trivial, divide a regular meromorphic section by the rational function realizing the triviality to obtain a section t with zero divisor; it suffices to show that t trivializes the module, which may be checked etale locally.

Set up the local computation (proof lines 1283-1300): take an affine chart U on which the module is trivial and which is integral, write U as the spectrum of a normal Noetherian domain with fraction field K, and write the restriction of t as f times a trivialization with f in K; for a height one prime of A corresponding to a codimension one point of X choose a trivialization near that point and a geometric point over it, and identify the relevant strict henselizations as discrete valuation rings by normality.

Conclude that f is a unit on the chart (proof lines 1300-1320): comparing the two trivializations over the strict henselization shows that the local equation of t differs from f by a unit; the vanishing of the order of t along the corresponding prime divisor forces that local equation to be a unit, hence f is a unit in the strict henselization and in particular in the localization of A at the height one prime; the intersection lemma for normal domains then puts f in A, so t is a global section.

Finish (proof lines 1320-1326): repeating the argument with t inverse viewed as a meromorphic section of the dual module shows that the inverse is also a global section, so t is a trivialization and the class of the module in the Picard group is trivial.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a meromorphic section with zero divisor.
Check triviality etale locally, writing the section over a normal affine chart as a rational function times a trivialization.

Compare local equations over a discrete valuation ring at a codimension one point and use the intersection theorem for normal domains to conclude that the function is regular, then repeat for the inverse.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a locally Noetherian integral normal algebraic space the canonical map from the Picard group to the divisor class group is injective (statement lines 1262-1267). The proof (proof lines 1269-1329) reduces to showing that a meromorphic section with zero divisor trivializes the module, checks this etale locally over an integral affine chart, compares local equations over a discrete valuation ring at a codimension one point, and uses the intersection theorem for normal domains to conclude that the section and its inverse are global. H3: a long local-global argument with genuine valuation theoretic computations, written out in full.
